clue.text: Bad morning, so good to be inside the House

indicators.note: the good letter is told to sit within the royal house, so it goes inside that name

parts.note: the House of Hanover, the royal dynasty of Georgian Britain

explanation.surface: Someone wakes feeling rough after a late night in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be inside' puts G within HANOVER. 'the House' looks like Parliament but is a royal house, Hanover, which ruled Britain from 1714 to 1901.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the miserable morning after heavy drinking, hence a bad start to the day.

clue.text: Hold up greetings card

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
the jack is a court card in a pack

explanation.surface: A greetings card is being held up for display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' reads as displaying a card, but it is the robbery sense: seizing a vehicle by force.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize a vehicle or plane by force, a kind of armed robbery or hold-up.

clue.text: One constantly finds fault with it for a penny in the pound

indicators.note: the clue puts the word it and the penny inside the slang pound, so they go in

parts.note: nicker is British slang for a pound sterling
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A fussy person complains about a deduction of a penny in every pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicker is British slang for a pound sterling; 'One constantly finds fault' is the definition, while 'for' and 'with' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitpicker is a pedant who keeps finding petty flaws in others' work.

clue.text: Fruit that's round, as it happens

parts.note: O is round in shape
a live broadcast goes out as it happens, in real time

explanation.surface: A round fruit is described in real time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' is the broadcasting sense, live rather than recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is the small stone fruit of the Mediterranean olive tree.

clue.text: Once broke, nothing for me but providence

indicators.note: broke signals that the letters of the first word are smashed and rearranged

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
me and my are interchangeable in exclamations such as 'dear me' and 'oh my'

explanation.surface: Someone once penniless now trusts only in their own careful foresight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' turns ONCE into ECON; add O and MY. 'providence' is used in its old sense of thrift, not divine care.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence in the sense of frugal foresight is thrift, careful management of money.

clue.text: Mark on a black beetle

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone notices a mark on a black beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Cut and paste one of two eating utensils

parts.note: to chop is to cut
to stick is to paste or glue

explanation.surface: A computer user's cut and paste commands sit oddly beside cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and paste' reads as the editing command, but it is two separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopsticks are a pair of thin sticks used for eating in East Asia, so one stick is half the set.

clue.text: Bemoan exercise that's restricted Asian currency

indicators.note: the exercise is restricted, hemmed in by the word for bemoan around it

parts.note: to rue is to bemoan or regret
PE is physical education, exercise at school

explanation.surface: Someone laments that their exercise is limited, mentioning money in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted' is the container signal: the exercise sits inside the word for bemoan, and 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the money of India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal.

clue.text: Something that may be flying, other than hair

parts.note: but means except, other than, as in 'all but one'
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Something flies, apart from hair blowing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' points at birds or planes, but a flying buttress is the arched support on Gothic churches.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying buttress is an arched masonry prop against a cathedral wall, so this support can be 'flying'.

clue.text: Eject, though plane is not to crash

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: crashing wrecks the words before it, so their letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A pilot ejects even though the aircraft is not going down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crash' anagrams 'is not'; 'though' is only a link, and the surface's pilot ejecting misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, to cast out.

clue.text: Threaten to put butter on dung

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate or threaten
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: Someone is warned not to spread butter on manure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put ... on' is just the joining instruction: the butter goes after the threat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowpat is a round flat dropping of cattle dung.

clue.text: Looks up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same going up as going down, a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone looks someone else up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' sounds like looking a person over, but says the answer reads the same either way in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to look at, so sees means looks.

clue.text: Country where you'll catch cold

parts.note: a South American country whose name is said like a word for cold weather, chilly

explanation.surface: A traveller warns that visiting a certain nation brings a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The country's name sounds like 'chilly', though Chile is far from cold throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is the long thin South American country, whose name is pronounced like chilly.

clue.text: To reverse wildly, for example?

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of the two words before it are thrown about

explanation.surface: A driver backs up recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges TO REVERSE; the whole clue then describes a car swinging too sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversteer is a car turning more sharply than the driver intends, the rear sliding out, as in a wild manoeuvre.

clue.text: Revealing spy novel must be purchased

indicators.note: what is purchased is taken in, so the spy takes in the novel's title

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel

explanation.surface: A gripping spy novel is a must-buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be purchased' has SPY take in KIM, Kipling's novel, which is itself about a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothes are scanty and show a lot of the body.

clue.text: Isle that turns to an island

parts.note: the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: turns says the letters of that are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: One isle transforms into another island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges THAT into HATT; 'to' is a link. Manhattan is the island at the heart of New York City.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is an island bounded by the Hudson and East rivers.

clue.text: Trembles with cold, when for two seconds Parisian winter's closed in

indicators.note: the French winter is shut in between the two seconds placed around it

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second, taken twice
hiver is French for winter

explanation.surface: Someone shivers when a Paris winter briefly closes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closed in' puts HIVER between S and S; 'Parisian' signals French.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivering is the shaking of the body when chilled.

clue.text: Count and Queen dined after ordering menu

indicators.note: the queen and dined come after the reshuffled menu
ordering puts the letters of menu into a new sequence

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
ate means dined

explanation.surface: A count and a queen eat after ordering from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' rearranges MENU and 'after' says the queen and dining follow. 'Count' is the verb, not the nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to list one by one, to tally.

clue.text: Food this compiler audibly shouts for?

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, I

indicators.note: audibly says the setter's whole cry is to be heard, the spoken phrase then spelt as something else

parts.note: screams are shouts

explanation.surface: The setter yells in hunger for some food.
explanation.walkthrough: From the rhyme 'I scream, you scream, we all scream for ice cream': 'I scream' said aloud runs into the frozen dessert, the S shifting to end the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen dessert made of sweetened cream.

clue.text: Crown of gold, one seen in court

indicators.note: gold and one are seen inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A gold crown is on show in a royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal; 'of' is a link. OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by nobles.

clue.text: Show disapproval of posh frock

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
U is the label for upper-class usage, posh

explanation.surface: Someone frowns on an upper-class dress.
explanation.walkthrough: U-and-non-U was a 1950s British label for upper-class and middle-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the stiff short skirt worn by ballerinas.

clue.text: Reconcile with the constitution

definitions.meaning: two people who ... are reconciled after a quarrel
someone's ... is their nature or physical constitution

explanation.surface: Settling differences, with talk of the nation's founding document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constitution' looks political, but it means a person's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up is to patch up a quarrel, and make-up also means one's basic composition.

clue.text: Game lost by the witless?

definitions.meaning: a children's game played with small glass balls
to lose your ... is to go mad, losing your wits

explanation.surface: A match is lost by those without any sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to lose one's marbles' means to go mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbles is a game of rolling glass balls, and marbles stands for one's sanity in the idiom.

clue.text: Shy and reserved, so drink

indicators.note: reserved means held back, so the word shy keeps the word and inside it

explanation.surface: A shy, reserved person settles for a mild drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserved' looks like a synonym of 'Shy' but is the container signal. Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a drink of beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Letter, or card

definitions.meaning: a single written symbol such as A or B
an eccentric or amusing person, a real card

explanation.surface: Choosing between writing a letter or sending a card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' is the old sense of a joker or eccentric person, not a greetings card.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a letter or symbol in writing, and also an odd or amusing person.

clue.text: Daisy's behind not entirely visible

indicators.note: only part of the word for behind shows, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: astern means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Daisy's bottom is only partly on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy's' reads as a girl's name, but means 'Daisy is'. 'not entirely visible' cuts ASTERN to ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The aster is a daisy-like flower of the family Asteraceae.

clue.text: European provides sound payment

indicators.note: sound tells you to say the payment word aloud and spell it as another word

parts.note: a cheque is a written order for payment

explanation.surface: A European offers a sound payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective (reliable payment) but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a native of the Czech Republic in central Europe.

clue.text: Passage that's sensual, not right

indicators.note: not right asks for the right abbreviation to be dropped from the word

parts.note: carnal means of the flesh, sensual

explanation.surface: A passage described as sensual, yet improper.
explanation.walkthrough: R is right; 'not right' removes it from CARNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made waterway, a passage for boats.

clue.text: Property makes the English panic

parts.note: to be in a state is to be in a panic

explanation.surface: Buying property sends the English into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' is British for flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of land or property owned by one person.

clue.text: Insect found in unsweetened fruit

indicators.note: the insect is found inside the word for unsweetened

parts.note: plain food has nothing added, such as sugar
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect turns up in some unsweetened fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is the container signal; plain yoghurt or plain biscuits are the unsweetened sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The plantain is a starchy cooking banana.

clue.text: Remain at sea? That's his job!

definitions.text: Remain at sea? That's his job!

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of remain are muddled

explanation.surface: Someone's job is to stay out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges REMAIN; the whole clue then describes a sailor-soldier's duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A marine is a soldier serving on board a ship, whose work keeps him on the waves.

clue.text: Instrument of rest and play

indicators.note: of here means made from, the instrument being built out of the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A musical instrument for relaxing and playing.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of REST and PLAY rearrange to give it; 'of' says the instrument is made from them.
explanation.definitionFit: The psaltery is an ancient plucked stringed instrument, like a zither.
